Dionysius Thrax ( Ancient Greek : Διονύσιος ὁ Θρᾷξ , romanized : Dionýsios ho Thrâix , 170–90 BC) was a Greek [ 1 ] grammarian and a pupil of Aristarchus of Samothrace . He was long considered to be the author of the earliest grammatical text on the Greek language, one that was used as a standard manual for perhaps some 1,500 years, [ 2 ] and which was until recently regarded as the groundwork of the entire Western grammatical tradition. [ a ]
